title: In Bengal, Tribunal Remedy has Been Slowest Where the SIR Has Affected Muslim Voters the Most
summary: Highlights that out of the 72,05,162 names found 'not eligible to vote', 18.98 lakh were Muslims based on a RTI response. Malda and Murshidabad districts share 6,83,683 exclusions, out of this 6,52,858 were Muslims. 16 constituencies across the state had no restorations. In Uttar Dinajpur, 90.4% marked not eligible were Muslims. However, it also showed faster decisions at the Tribunal level in comparison to Malda and Murshidabad.

title: Election Commission's appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
summary: More than 16 lakh voters who were excluded in SIR in West Bengal were cleared by judicial officers. However, the Election Commission of India filed appeals against the exclusions. However, the officials who filed the appeals might not have the authority to do that as under the Representation of the People Act.Only the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are authorized. The Election Commission in its affidavit to the Supreme Court said that the 'officers had the authority to file the appeals as per the order of this Hon'ble (Supreme) Court.'But the affidavit only mentions authorities as per the Representation of People Act.

title: SIR: ECI moves to strike off 76,000 judge-cleared voters in Bengal's border seats, nearly all Muslim names
summary:
The Election Commission of India appealed against the judicial officers' decision in two constituencies in West Bengal, Murshidabad and Malda which had cleared 76,000 voters. Mostly all the names excluded are commonly associated with the Muslim community (99.9% in Samserganj and 99.6% in Sujapur). If these appeals are upheld, the constituencies could see a reduction in the number of voters cleared by the judicial officers. Further, in Samserganj, the officers deleted 69% (1,08,400) voters under adjudication leaving only 33,152 on the rolls. ECI appealed against 15,195 of these exclusions. In Sujapur, of the 1,34,521 voters under adjudication judgers deleted only 20% and cleared the rest 1,07,690. ECI challeneged the inclusion of 56.7% (61,066) of them. This means Samserganj would lose a total of 83% voters placed under adjudication and Sujapur would lose 65%.
Samserganj has approximately 72% Muslim population while Sujapur has 75%.

title: In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses
summary: Mustafabad constituency in Delhi saw the highest number of Form 7 applications with 843 objections (since August 31). Further, of the 597 objection forms filed by third parties, 96% named BJP's booth level agents (BLA) as 'objectors'. Further, 572 Form 7s are filed against Muslims electors across the constituency. It excludes people living in the area for over two decades. A total of 28 voters were sought to be deleted from the area citing 'absent/ permanently shift' or 'death' as the reason.' All of the electors were found to be living in the area at their addresses. Further, 10 BLAs filed more than 30 Form 7 and 9s over 25 applications. However, ECI's directive of October 9 only permits a cap of 10 forms per individual elector. BLAs can submit up to 10 forms a day including Forms 6, 7 and 8 which are filled by individual electors. They are also required to submit a list of applications with an undertaking that they verified the details. The BLAs also gave no undertaking about the objections the filed. The people against whom the objections were filed said they do not know who the person is (objector has to be a registered elector in the constituency). One of the objectors initially said he resides in the area, then said he did not file the objections and is not a BLA or associated with any political party.

title: Over 340 voter ID cards found on Narmada riverbank in MP's Khargone, Congress seeks FIR
summary: 343 voter ID cards with addresses of Indore were found at the Narmada riverbank in Khargone district in Madhya Pradesh. The cards belong to the Rau constituency and the addresses listed on Electoral Photo ID Cards (EPICs) include Tilak Nagar and Aastha Palace. It was alleged that the card carried 2016 as the year however, the digital card format was introduced in 2021. Similar discoveries were also made in Chhatarpur, another district in Madhya Pradesh where hundreds of voter ID cards were found in October 2025 in the Raja Talab.

title: Testimony of a single mother excluded in the SIR Process
summary: It is unclear where the woman if from. She is a single mother who was excluded in the SIR process. She shared her experience during the public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar. She got to know that her vote was deleted and how she used it as an identity card for scholarships and opening bank account. She is an Indian citizen and she says she has to work and this way, the government is creating ways for her to just stand in long queues. If she has to stand in another queue, how will she get her daughter educated and how will she plan her future.
